sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Dyer’s greenweed (Genista tinctoria) is an upright subshrub native from Europe to southwestern Siberia and Afghanistan. It is usually 60–100 cm tall.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Its yellow pea-shaped flowers grow in clusters; the flattened pods are about 1.5–3 cm long. The plant was cultivated as a source of yellow dye.

sections.title: Caution
sections.text: Botanical sources report toxicity. Despite historical mentions of eating flower buds, consumption is not recommended.
